name: Adafruit STEMMA Reflective Photo Interrupt Sensor
description: Adafruit breakout for the Vishay TCRT1000 reflective optical sensor (950 nm IR LED plus phototransistor behind a daylight filter, peak at 1 mm, useful 0.2-4 mm). The IR LED is always on, its current set by a trimmer from about 10 mA to about 100 mA. The phototransistor collector is SIG, pulled up to VIN by 10 kOhm: HIGH with nothing in front, pulled toward 0 V (LOW) when IR is reflected back; a red Sig LED lights while SIG is low and a green ON LED shows power. Runs on 3-5 V. Sold as: Adafruit STEMMA Reflective Photo Interrupt Sensor - TCRT1000 (product 5913; listed in the request as #5629, which is actually a different Adafruit product), 3-pin header SIG, VIN, GND plus a matching STEMMA JST PH connector.
eli5: Shines invisible infrared light out of its tip and tells your board when something very close (a few millimetres) bounces it back, so you can spot an object, a slot edge or filament passing by.

pins.name: SIG
pins.description: Signal output (header pin 1, white JST wire): TCRT1000 phototransistor collector with a 10 kOhm pull-up to VIN. HIGH with nothing detected, LOW while IR is reflected back (red Sig LED on). Swings to VIN, so power the board from 3.3 V on a 3.3 V microcontroller.

pins.name: VIN
pins.description: Supply (header pin 2, red JST wire): 3-5 V, same as the microcontroller's logic level. Use 3V3 with an ESP32 or Pico because SIG is pulled up to VIN.

supplierQuery: Adafruit 5913 STEMMA Reflective Photo Interrupt Sensor TCRT1000
buildNotes: Header order as printed on the board: SIG, VIN, GND. The STEMMA JST PH connector carries the same signals (white SIG, red VIN, black GND).
Power VIN from 3.3 V on an ESP32 or Pico: SIG is pulled up to VIN through 10 kOhm, so a 5 V supply would put 5 V on the GPIO.
SIG is HIGH with nothing in front and LOW while IR is reflected back (red Sig LED lights).
The TCRT1000 only sees things very close: best at about 1 mm, usable from 0.2 to 4 mm.
The trimmer sets the IR LED current from about 10 mA to about 100 mA: turn it up for more sensitivity. At full current the board draws about 100 mA, which the 3V3 pin of an ESP32 or Pico can supply.
Cut the On / Sig jumpers on the back to disable the green power LED or the red signal LED.
Sunlight contains IR and can cause false detections.

driver.code:
# Adafruit STEMMA Reflective Photo Interrupt Sensor (product 5913, Vishay TCRT1000), MicroPython driver.
# Board circuit (Adafruit "Stemma TCRT1000 rev A" schematic):
#   IR LED: anode through the 200 ohm trimmer R5 and R2 to VIN, always on. The trimmer sets the LED
#   current from about 10 mA (least sensitive) to about 100 mA (most sensitive).
#   Phototransistor: emitter to GND, collector = SIG, pulled up to VIN by R4 (10 kOhm).
#   Red "Sig" LED (via R1) from VIN to SIG lights when SIG is pulled low.
# So: nothing in front -> transistor off -> SIG HIGH (= VIN).
#     IR bounced back by an object / light surface (best at about 1 mm, 0.2-4 mm) -> SIG pulled toward 0 V -> LOW.
# SIG swings up to VIN: on a 3.3 V board (ESP32, Pico) power VIN from 3.3 V.
from machine import Pin


class StemmaReflective:
    def __init__(self, sig_pin):
        # SIG already has a 10 kOhm pull-up to VIN on the board.
        self.sig = Pin(sig_pin, Pin.IN) if isinstance(sig_pin, int) else sig_pin

    def raw(self):
        """Logic level on SIG: 0 = reflection detected, 1 = nothing detected."""
        return self.sig.value()

    def detected(self):
        """True while IR is reflected back into the phototransistor (object / light surface close in front)."""
        return self.sig.value() == 0

    def irq(self, handler, on_detect=True):
        """Call handler(pin) when an object appears (falling edge) or, with on_detect=False,
        when it goes away (rising edge)."""
        trig = Pin.IRQ_FALLING if on_detect else Pin.IRQ_RISING
        return self.sig.irq(handler=handler, trigger=trig)

example.code:
from stemma_reflective import StemmaReflective
import time

sensor = StemmaReflective({SIG})
while True:
    print('Object: %s' % ('yes' if sensor.detected() else 'no'))
    time.sleep(0.2)

test.title: Reports an object when IR is reflected back
